---- page 1 ----
INT. MARA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Rain streaks the window. MARA (30s, exhausted) stares at an
unplugged phone. She has been staring at it for what feels
like hours, and the well-known silence of the room presses
in.

                      MARA
                (to herself)
          He is not going to call. He is not
          going to call, and that is fine,
          because I am fine.

The phone lights up. She does not move.

                      JONAH (V.O.)
          Mara, it's me. I know it's late. I
          know you said not to, and I tried
          not to, I really did, but there is
          something I should have told you in
          the spring and I have been carrying
          it around ever since like a stone
          in my coat.

                      MARA
          Don't.

                                                     CUT TO:

EXT. ROOFTOP - CONTINUOUS

WIDE ON THE CITY

Wind. A water tower groans. JONAH (40s, coat collar up)
paces the length of the roof with the phone pressed to his
ear, listening to it ring out. He tries again. And again. On
the fourth try the line connects, and he stops dead, one
foot on the low parapet.

                      JONAH
          You picked up.

                      MARA (O.S.)
          I did not. The phone is face down
          on the table. I can hear you
          through the floor.

Jonah looks down. Directly beneath his boots, the skylight
glows yellow. Behind it, a woman sits very still.

INT. MARA'S APARTMENT - CONTINUOUS

Mara looks up at the skylight. Jonah's shadow falls across
the table, over the phone, over her hands. Neither of them
---- page 2 ----
says anything for a long time. The rain gets louder, then
softer, then stops as if somebody had closed a door on it.

                      MARA
                (finally)
          You can come down. The door is
          open. It has been open since March,
          and I would like you to understand
          that I am not saying that to be
          kind, I am saying it because I am
          tired of locking it every night and
          then lying awake listening for the
          sound of you not turning the
          handle.

                      JONAH
          I'm not sure I can.

                      MARA
          Then stay up there and freeze, I
          suppose.

                                               SMASH CUT TO:

EXT. ROOFTOP - LATER

The roof is empty. A single boot print in the wet tar,
pointing at the stairwell door.

                                                   FADE OUT.
